day_shape: CENTCOM reports 94 vessels redirected under US blockade of Iran as IRGC commanders claim control of Hormuz; Houthis wound 73+ in Saudi strikes; IAEA chief Grossi tells Board it has been blind to Iran's program since June 2025.

threads.label: US blockade and Hormuz standoff
threads.summary: CENTCOM said as of Sept 7 it had redirected 94 commercial vessels, disabled three and boarded two enforcing the US blockade against Iran in the Arabian Sea, while Jerusalem Post reported Hormuz shipping had slowed. IRGC deputy commander Izadi and SNSC secretary Rezaei claimed full Iranian control over the Strait and capability to target US carriers.

threads.label: Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia
threads.summary: Iran-backed Houthis attacked energy facilities and cities in southern Saudi Arabia, wounding at least 73 people according to the Saudi-led coalition. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed a "unique" missile and drone operation, while Yemeni government forces reported limited gains near the Red Sea and Saudi border.

threads.label: IAEA on Iran and regional nuclear files
threads.summary: IAEA Director-General Rafael Grossi told the Board of Governors the agency has been blind to Iran's nuclear program since at least June 2025, and said the Syrian reactor destroyed by Israel in 2007 could have quickly produced weapons-grade material. Saudi Arabia is preparing to allow IAEA inspections at its civil nuclear facilities under a US agreement.

threads.label: South Lebanon clashes and IDF strikes
threads.summary: The IDF said Hezbollah launched two explosive drones at troops in the Ali Taher Ridge for the third time in a week, and two soldiers were lightly wounded in a Beaufort-area gunfight before Israel struck weapons stores and infrastructure across south Lebanon. Lebanese civil defence, cited by IRIB, said 10 were killed and seven wounded in strikes on Kafr Raman.

threads.label: Gaza strikes and ISF plan
threads.summary: The IDF announced the killing of Hamas Nukhba company commander Yusuf Aqila and two further operatives in Gaza strikes, and said it diverted a munition mid-air after spotting civilians near a target. Kosovo signed on to join the International Stabilization Force in Gaza, while the US pushed a Board of Peace plan to decommission Hamas weapons paired with an Israeli withdrawal.

threads.label: Iranian domestic repression and dissent
threads.summary: Iran's judiciary confirmed the detention of hardline cleric Mohammad-Bagher Kharrazi and spokesman Kazemi said cases against "traitors" have produced indictments and large asset seizures, while former president Rouhani drew hardliner calls for arrest after urging public input on ending the war. Iran International reported oil-worker protests in Assaluyeh, small pensioner rallies in Tehran, and two suicides linked to families of slain January protesters.

threads.label: October 7 pre-warning claims
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar warned Netanyahu less than a week before October 7 that Hamas was "preparing something extreme" and urged approval to assassinate Yahya Sinwar. Naftali Bennett confirmed a Haaretz report on the warning, and a further report alleged UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed also warned Netanyahu days before the attack.

He, who entered university with rank 10 in the national entrance exam and rank 1 in the war-affected quota, emphasised that quota is not a substitute for effort and will never choose permanent emigration.
